title: One error fails the whole set
statement: In a set of questions judged together, one factual error can fail the whole set, so check each question on its own before the set is judged.
example: When factual accuracy failed in one model's question sets, nine other scored dimensions failed with it.
detail: In one fine-tuned model's results, when a question set failed on factual accuracy, nine other dimensions, from educational accuracy to integrity, failed with it (`icloud-work/ap-social-studies-generator/data/model_findings.md`). The generator's notes list a set in which one question had a documented factual error among its ten persistent failure cells, and name per-question independent validation as what it needs (`icloud-work/ap-social-studies-generator/python/CLAUDE.md`).
against: the same findings leave open whether the cascade is the evaluator's own failure mode or the sets were that flawed.

evidence.quote: MCQ_SET hard-fail dimensions cascade: when factual_accuracy fails, educational_accuracy, concept_coverage, localization_quality, difficulty_distribution, non_repetitiveness, test_preparedness, answer_balance, stimulus_quality, and integrity_check all fail together.
